claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and secret s in Z/NZ, the sample-only arbitrary-order Kuperberg algorithm described in proof.md recovers s with probability greater than 2/3 using total sequential work O(2^(10 sqrt(n)) n^10), where n=ceil(log2 N). Its exact time growth index is 1/2.
For the same algorithm and fixed configuration in proof.md, peak allocated classical space is O(2^(10 sqrt(n)) n^10) bits uniformly for all N and s. Its exact growth index is 1/2.
For the same algorithm and fixed configuration in proof.md, peak allocated quantum space is O(2^(10 sqrt(n)) n^10) qubits uniformly for all N and s. Its exact growth index is 1/2.

For the same algorithm and fixed configuration in proof.md, the number Q of fresh ideal DCP source copies is O(2^(10 sqrt(n)) n^10) uniformly for all N and s, counting discarded samples, filtering, batches, and verification copies. Its exact growth index is 1/2.
The algorithm's guarantee assumes all acquired source copies are independent ideal DCP coset states; the claimed fractional malformed-sample tolerance is zero.

structured.error_model: The guarantee requires every acquired copy to be an independent ideal DCP coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
